posts.title: ETH · Payy bridge exploit $1.83M
posts.caption:
Payy Network Halts After $1.83M Exploit

An attacker exploited Payy’s Ethereum bridge through a malicious verifyRollup transaction at 04:21 UTC. The stolen USDC was routed through Railgun, swapped for about 683 ETH and split across multiple wallets. Payy suspended deposits, withdrawals, transfers and card payments after its bridge was drained.

posts.title: FBI $150K reward · Khalid Ahmed Sattari
posts.caption:
The FBI has announced a $150,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of one of the most wanted fraudsters in the United States, Khalid Ahmed Sattari.

According to the investigation, between 2016 and 2019, he orchestrated a large-scale fraud scheme involving the federal Medicare program. Through a network of call centers, medical companies, intermediaries, and doctors, bills were submitted for unnecessary genetic tests.

The estimated damage is approximately $547 million.

posts.title: UK police seize $1.4M BTC from darknet markets

UK Police seized $1.4M in Bitcoin linked to defunct darknet markets.

posts.title: Callum Dyer (KT), Doxbin admin, 2y3m prison
posts.caption:
Doxbin administrator sentenced to 2 years and 3 months in prison

26-year-old Callum Dyer (KT) from Wales was sentenced for aiding attacks with false emergency calls (swatting) as a Doxbin administrator.

The investigation began after the FBI transferred data to British police in 2019. Investigators identified Dyer and found evidence on his devices of involvement in swatting and a phishing kit.

According to the prosecution, Dyer coordinated participants of the #deadnet channel, encouraging the conduct of new attacks. He pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 2 years and 3 months of imprisonment.

posts.title: Peter Stokes, Scattered Spider, extradited Finland → USA
posts.caption:
Vibe-hacker played himself.

19-year-old Peter Stokes, a citizen of the USA and Estonia, was extradited from Finland to the USA, where he will be tried on charges of participating in the hacker group Scattered Spider. He was arrested back in April right at the airport before a flight to Japan. During a search, two hard drives with evidence were found, which, according to the prosecution, indicate his involvement in cyberattacks.

Stokes himself did not hide his love for a luxurious life: he regularly posted photos from expensive hotels in Paris, Dubai and other cities on social media, demonstrating stacks of cash, jewelry, and even a diamond chain with the inscription "Hack the Planet".

The irony is that the charges feature the hacking of a major jewelry network. According to the investigation, the perpetrators stole the company's data and demanded about $8 million in cryptocurrency. The ransom was not paid, however, the damage to the business exceeded $2 million.

The group Scattered Spider (also known as Octo Tempest, UNC3944 and 0ktapus) is considered one of the most dangerous in recent years. It is linked to high-profile attacks on MGM Resorts, Caesars Entertainment and the British Marks & Spencer. According to the prosecution, the participants have more than 100 successful hacks and over $100 million obtained through extortion on their record.

posts.title: Tectonic exploit $75M
posts.caption:
Tectonic Exploit Sends $75M Into Chaos

On August 30 Tectonic on Cronos suffered a major exploit after an attacker manipulated the low liquidity TONIC governance token pushing its price nearly 100x in under 20 minutes. The inflated value was then used as collateral to borrow assets from the protocol
Around $6.29M was moved to Ethereum and converted into more than 2,600 ETH. An estimated $68.7M remains on Cronos where the affected funds have been paused. The attacker later sent 2,659 ETH to Tornado Cash making the trail harder to follow.

Separately PeckShieldAlert and Specter reported a possible exploit of Notional Finance’s escrow contract. The incident allegedly resulted in approximately $1.7M in DAI and USDC being stolen. The attacker then swapped the assets for 689.2 ETH and deposited the funds into Tornado Cash further complicating the tracking and recovery process. The two incidents show how quickly stolen assets can be converted and moved across networks after an exploit.
The exploit began with TONIC’s price being artificially inflated nearly 100x

posts.title: Italian police bust fake €2 coin ring
posts.caption:
Italian police bust fake €2 coin ring

Three Chinese nationals were arrested in Italy over suspicions of running a large-scale operation producing counterfeit €2 coins.

Investigators say that since late 2025, the group circulated around 20,000 fake coins, which were used in arcade machines to exchange for real cash.

The counterfeit coins were reportedly manufactured with materials smuggled from China and were highly sophisticated, closely matching genuine coins in weight, size, and magnetic properties.

posts.title: "Batman" ATM heist fails (2:05)
posts.caption:
"Batman" and friends fail ATM heist after excavator breaks down

A group of thieves in Tobago stole an excavator and tried to rip an ATM out of a bank before loading it into a truck.

The plan fell apart when the excavator's boom malfunctioned, forcing the suspects to abandon the robbery empty-handed after spending more than 10 minutes at the scene.

One of the suspects was dressed in a black cape and mask, earning the nickname "Batman" from local media.

Andrew and Tristan Tate arrested in Miami

posts.title: ZachXBT refuses to investigate Coldcard hack
posts.caption:
ZachXBT refuses to investigate Coldcard hack

On-chain investigator ZachXBT said he will not investigate the Coldcard wallet hack, criticizing the Bitcoin community for not supporting his work.

He pointed to a previous case where he tracked a ~$600K theft and helped freeze ~$96K, but the victim refused to contact police due to tax concerns and later ignored a $5K payment request for his investigation work.

posts.title: ZachXBT $10K bounty replying to Vova Sadkov
posts.caption:
Who is ZachXBT and how was he doxxed?

ZachXBT is a well-known crypto investigator who publishes exposés on scammers and hackers.

In 2026, users linked his account to Zachary Wolk after this name appeared in court documents. Using open sources and OSINT, researchers found a number of matches regarding age, place of residence, and biography.

After the doxxing, the community began discussing his methods of work, funding, and possible conflicts of interest. ZachXBT himself remains one of the most influential figures in crypto investigations.
